title: Power Pages: OpenID Connect sign-in accepts encrypted ID tokens
summary: The briefing accurately reports the roadmap plans and distinguishes existing authentication controls from undocumented encrypted-token settings. The provider-editing path needs only a minor clarification to include the More Commands menu and Additional settings heading.

claims.where: title; summary; What's changing; Risk assessment; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The roadmap plans acceptance of encrypted ID tokens in addition to signed tokens.
claims.quote: This feature adds support for token-level encryption during authentication, allowing Power Pages to accept encrypted ID tokens in addition to signed tokens.

claims.claim: The item is listed under the Power Pages design studio.
claims.quote: Power Pages: Design studio - Enhance OpenID Connect with encrypted token support

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; rationale: impact
claims.claim: The change is intended to improve compatibility with identity providers requiring stronger token security.
claims.quote: improves compatibility with advanced identity providers

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; rationale: risk; rationale: impact

claims.quote: strengthens overall authentication security without changing existing sign-in flows.

claims.claim: An ID token is a security token that lets a client verify a user's identity.
claims.quote: An ID token is a security token that allows a client to verify the identity of a user.

claims.claim: An ID token carries claims such as an email address.

claims.claim: Authentication setting changes might take a few minutes to appear on a site.

claims.claim: The authentication governance path is Power Platform admin center > Manage > Products > Power Pages > Settings > Authentication > OpenID Connect > environment > Manage > site preference.
claims.quote:
Under Authentication, select the authentication option you want to manage.
Select an environment, and then select Manage.
Choose the sites where makers can configure the authentication option.

claims.claim: The OpenID Connect protocol control governs OpenID Connect providers on targeted sites within an environment.
claims.quote:
Each protocol control determines whether makers can configure identity providers that use that protocol on the targeted sites.
OpenID Connect | OpenID Connect (OIDC) identity providers, including Microsoft Entra External ID.

claims.claim: Blocking OpenID Connect prevents makers configuring providers that use that protocol.
claims.quote: In the design studio, a protocol or identity provider that governance blocks appears dimmed and can't be configured.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance controls
claims.claim: Blocking OpenID Connect prevents users signing in through that protocol.
claims.quote: When a governance setting that blocks an authentication option takes effect, users can no longer sign in or register by using that authentication option.

claims.claim: The site preference can allow the authentication option for all sites in the environment.

claims.claim: The site preference can allow the authentication option for all sites except selected sites.
claims.quote: All sites except specific sites | Makers can configure the option for every site except the sites you select.

claims.claim: The site preference can allow the authentication option only for selected sites.

claims.claim: Existing OpenID Connect provider claims mappings are reached in design studio through Security > Identity providers > provider > Edit configuration > Registration claims mapping / Login claims mapping.
claims.quote:
Additional settings in Power Pages
Registration claims mapping and Login claims mapping
claims.fix: In controls[1].ui.path and the rendered row, use 'Security > Identity providers > provider > More Commands (...) > Edit configuration > Additional settings > Registration claims mapping / Login claims mapping'. The editing route is documented at the already-cited https://learn.microsoft.com/power-pages/security/authentication/configure-site#edit-an-identity-provider; the setting labels are at https://learn.microsoft.com/power-pages/security/authentication/openid-provider.

claims.claim: Power Pages licensing is capacity based.
claims.quote: Power Pages (formerly Power Apps portals) licensing is capacity based and offers two types of capacities based on user type: Authenticated users per website/month and Anonymous users per website/month.

claims.claim: Authenticated website access can use the Authenticated user capacity subscription license.
claims.quote: The Authenticated user capacity subscription license can be purchased for the anticipated number of unique, authenticated users.
